item.title: Digital illiteracy: key figures
item.description:
In short:

  1. In France, 15% of the population aged 15 and over is in a situation of digital illiteracy according to Insee, for lack of basic digital skills or internet use.
  2. The phenomenon rises sharply with age: 2% of 15-24 year-olds against 62% of those aged 75 and over.
  3. 29% of French people completed no dematerialised administrative procedure in twelve months, a share that rises to 58% among people with no qualifications.
  4. For a local authority, the response rests as much on the design of online procedures as on the human support that remains necessary.

Digital illiteracy refers to the difficulty or inability to use digital tools independently. Used for several years in public studies, it has become widespread as services, both public and private, have made digital use a condition of access.

item.title: Why online procedures at town halls plateau
item.description:
In short:

  1. Digitising a form does not digitise the processing it triggers: if that stays manual, the delay does not move.
  2. An online procedure with no quick answer adds a channel instead of removing one, because the user calls back or visits.
  3. The order of digitisation matters: start with high-volume procedures that have standardised processing.
  4. The useful indicator is the share of cases completed without further contact, not the number of forms opened.

The first factor: the processing behind

An online procedure has two halves. The first is visible: the form. The second is not: the handling of the case by a member of staff. Digitisation most often covers the first only.
